summary: Fortuna sits on the flat floor of the Eel River valley about fifteen miles south of Eureka, and its home-price-to-income ratio of roughly 5.7× — with a median home at $353,200 against a $61,603 median household income — is remarkably moderate for anywhere in California, where double-digit ratios dominate coastal metros. At just over 5 square miles and 12,000 residents, the town is compact enough that its main commercial strip along Fortuna Boulevard, the redwood-country river bars, and the surrounding dairy and ranch land all sit within a short drive of each other, giving everyday life a rhythm that is more small-town-practical than suburban-commuter. The economy leans on timber-related industries, healthcare (nearby St. Joseph Hospital system facilities in Eureka are a major regional employer), and public-sector jobs; switching employers without a 30-mile drive north to Eureka or south along US-101 is genuinely limited. Temperatures hover in a remarkably narrow band — average highs around 61°F year-round, lows near 46°F — meaning no real summer heat and no hard freezes, but also only about seven hours of sunshine a day on average, a reminder that the North Coast's famous redwood fog is a year-round companion. Median rent at $1,126 keeps housing accessible relative to income, yet the 16.8% poverty rate signals that the local wage base is thin, not that costs are trivially low. Fortuna is the rare California town where buying a home on the median income is arithmetically plausible — the tradeoff is geographic isolation and an economy with a narrow set of rungs.
